elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.4 carve-out (a) covers only "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities"; no affiliate assignment exception is granted to Customer, so an affiliate transfer still needs M&I's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "(a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities" (subject only to Section 21.11 compliance and written notice).

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained "(b) M&I may assign this Agreement (i) in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, or (ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division" — M&I keeps consent-free assignment rights.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained lead-in: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" — applies mutually, including to M&I assignments outside the (b) carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears anywhere in the rendered 22.4; M&I's (b) carve-outs are unrestricted as to assignee identity.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 21.11.B (unchanged): "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement" — obligation is only volume-limited (prior entities; prior 3-month volumes plus 25%), not a termination or re-pricing right. Section 11.3 is redacted but is carved out of Section 11.1 as a Customer right, so no Vendor trigger is visible.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer: carve-out (a) "to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities"; M&I: (b)(i) "in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities".

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted "provided that, in each case upon written notice to the other party" governs both (a) and (b); the word "freely" was struck from M&I's clause so the notice condition is not contradicted.

The retained proviso (b)(ii) lets M&I assign without Customer consent "to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I" — a divisional/partial-business transfer, not succession to M&I as an entity. That retained no-consent, non-successor exception defeats the element notwithstanding the general consent sentence. Repair: delete clause (b)(ii), or subject it to Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld), or narrow it to a successor to all or substantially all of M&I's business.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

reasons: Fallback is one element short: clause (b)(ii) survives and gives M&I a consent-free right to assign to a purchaser/successor of the M&I Data Services division — a partial-business transfer rather than succession to M&I itself. Because a no-consent non-successor exception is retained, "Other assignments require consent." is not met.

Actionable repair: strike "(ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I", or make that transfer subject to Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), or narrow it to a successor to all or substantially all of M&I's business (already covered by (b)(i)).

Preferred is not available on this draft: no Customer affiliate carve-out, M&I retains consent-free assignment rights, and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. Preferred element on change of control is, however, already satisfied by Section 21.11.B.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to broadening Customer's carve-out (removing the $100,000,000 financial-institution gate), adding the mutual written-notice condition, and deleting "freely" (necessary so M&I's carve-out is not inconsistent with the notice condition). The Section 21.11 cross-reference, the consent standard, and Section 21.11.B volume limits are retained.
Intent preserved: no dangling definitions or cross-references; Change-in-Control mechanics, Section 21.11 compliance condition, and M&I's existing carve-out structure survive without contradiction.

Note for the rationale (not a defect): Customer's broadened carve-out reaches sale of "assets, stock or securities", mirroring M&I's clause, which is consistent with the fallback's mutual-successor framing.
